Windows packaged QEMU boot and connection, audit 2325

Existing job invocation, from repository root:
  python .github/scripts/test-windows-vm-boot.py "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/windows-vm-boot"

Run in the existing native Windows x64 row. Allow a 26-minute step timeout and
at least 35 minutes for the row including its other tests. The fixture itself
has a 25-minute wall deadline, with shorter per-child and 10-minute boot bounds.
No new runner, Hyper-V, nested virtualization, privileged kernel setup, physical
board, user VM, package-manager install, or machine-wide PATH modification.

The required existing tools are Go, Python, Git, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and
7-Zip. GITHUB_ACTIONS must be true and output must be a fresh directory below
RUNNER_TEMP. The script refuses missing tools rather than installing them.
At least 12 GiB free space is required. QEMU uses ordinary software TCG and
user-mode networking; the guest is the actual published ARM64 WendyOS image.

Pinned inputs

* QEMU Windows x64 11.1.0, qemu-w64-setup-20260811.exe, 206615928 bytes,
  SHA256 f98a8aeb5f7faea9765b6dee28316c266cd179d80354a2fed8e50176f9a2e59f.
  Source: microsoft/winget-pkgs, SoftwareFreedomConservancy.QEMU/11.1.0
  installer manifest Git blob bb2abbb27f70181c27f27a1ec5ac5ec490000125.
  https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/blob/master/manifests/s/SoftwareFreedomConservancy/QEMU/11.1.0/SoftwareFreedomConservancy.QEMU.installer.yaml
  The script contains the exact HTTPS download URL. It extracts this NSIS
  package as data with 7-Zip; it never executes the installer or changes its
  registry/uninstaller state. All executable/DLL/firmware files remain inside
  the private Program Files directory. Actual emulator version and firmware
  size are checked before boot. Extracted executable/firmware hashes are retained.

* WendyOS vm-arm64 0.20.2, published wic.zst, 582023203 bytes,
  SHA256 f9f3e3ac18936230d1f72a38a097ba3bae5f7e37ccaba663b20dbfcc53849ea3.
  Source: https://storage.googleapis.com/wendyos-images-public/manifests/vm-arm64.json
  Published image path is pinned in the script, not resolved through latest.
  The image supplies the real guest kernel, firmware boot chain and Agent.
  This checks current CLI compatibility with that released Agent; it does not
  claim to boot an Agent rebuilt from the current WendyOS checkout.

Both downloads reject redirects/proxies and require exact byte length/SHA256.
A child-process deadline bounds slow headers and body reads as well as the
in-process size/time check. No download/hash failure is accepted as a skip.

Observed journey

The actual current CLI and historical control are built with the existing Go
cache. Candidate/source/artifact hashes and revision are retained. The CLI sees
a fresh WENDY_CONFIG_DIR and a PATH without QEMU, while ProgramFiles points to
the private extracted package. Thus discovery and firmware lookup must traverse
the real Windows installation-path fallback, including spaces in the path.

The CLI creates a private 16-GiB sparse VM from the pinned compressed image.
Before boot, the exact original Spec.Binary PATH-only behavior is restored in a
Go overlay and compiled. Its real CLI start must return structured tool_not_found exit 6 at the named missing
executable lookup, not at download/build/firmware/port validation. No assertion
or production source in the normal binary is altered.

The normal CLI starts the VM in the foreground with TCG and a dynamically chosen
adjacent port pair. The actual `--device vm:NAME device info --read-only --json` path must
connect to the guest Agent without upgrading/provisioning it and report vm-arm64, arm64, WendyOS 0.20.2 and an Agent
version. The Windows TCP table's listener PID must match the private run record,
and the process's executable path must match the pinned extracted QEMU. This
prevents an unrelated local Agent from satisfying a boot check.

The documented Ctrl-A x console sequence exits this foreground QEMU. This is an
intentional power-off of a disposable disk copy, not proof of guest graceful
shutdown. The original CLI must exit successfully, `vm list --json` must report
only this VM stopped, and both forwarded ports must be bindable again. The CLI
then removes only its stopped private VM without --force.

Ownership and retained results

A Python launcher waits for a fresh nonce before spawning anything. Its owner
assigns it to a retained kill-on-close Windows Job first, then writes that nonce.
All Go/compiler/extractor/CLI/QEMU children inherit the Job. Every command has a
deadline. Cancellation is recorded while the bounded Job drain runs; repeated
signals cannot interrupt cleanup. The final result is rejected on interruption
or unproven drain. No saved PID, global process-name kill, user config or user VM
is used for cleanup.

Upload only *.log and *.json from the output directory, not executables, package,
firmware or disk images. Preserve failed output until the owned Job has drained.
WINDOWS_VM_BOOT_VERIFIED plus evidence.json status passed and cleanup passed are
required. A cross-compile or offline Python pass is not a Windows boot result.
Native Windows runtime execution remains pending until the hosted gate runs.

This closes the boot/discovery requirement only after actual hosted success.
It does not exercise WinGet's machine-wide installer, interactive prompt rendering,
WSL2, physical USB, enrolled-agent TLS, or automatic Windows VM detachment (which
is explicitly unsupported in production). Existing installer-policy tests remain
separate from the real package extraction and VM boot proof.

VM lifecycle extension for2270/2060:
The same private guest now boots twice. The first foreground start omits --port
while the fixture owns a live listener on default50051. Actual CLI runstate,
metadata and kernel listener ownership must agree on a later bounded port span.
After Ctrl-A x joins the owned QEMU/CLI and both VM ports can be rebound, the
fixture closes only its default-port obstruction. Restarting the SAME disk with
--port still omitted must keep the saved fallback, create a new run timestamp,
reach the real pinned WendyOS Agent again and drain before removal. No extra
artifact download, VM disk, QEMU installation or runner is introduced; the same
25-minute overall deadline applies and must fail rather than skip an incomplete
second boot. Windows automatic detached start/QMP app forwarding is explicitly
unsupported in production; this does not pretend to exercise those Unix paths.

Schema and restart observations

Hosted job 131729254510 booted the exact pinned image and reached the Agent;
collision-info-38.log reported osVersion WendyOS-0.20.2. The fixture then failed
because it expected hostname/publicKey in CLI hardware JSON. Those fields are
not emitted there, and the Linux Agent does not populate the optional publicKey
RPC field. This correction does not claim a cryptographic device identity.

The CLI hardware assertion uses its actual exact OS-version spelling. After
checking the kernel listener owner, a separately built read-only helper calls
GetAgentVersion for the persistent hostname and GetNetworkStats for the actual
kernel boot ID and boot-time sample. The response must match the CLI's version,
OS, architecture and device type. The listener owner is checked again afterward.
The restarted guest must retain its hostname and the same owned disk file ID,
path and size, keep the previously asserted VM metadata/port, and return a new
nonzero kernel boot UUID and a new VM run timestamp. Both boots still require
foreground-process drain and forwarded-port reclamation. The helper has a
10-second RPC deadline and runs in the same retained Windows Job as the CLI.

Portable real gRPC tests and Windows cross-compilation verify the helper without
booting a VM. Full corrected native Windows lifecycle acceptance remains pending.
